newsitem.title: HUNGARY: FOCUS - Budapest bull run steals show in Cen Europe.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Budapest bull run steals show in Cen Europe.

text.p: The Budapest Stock Exchange outperformed other markets in the region this week, scoring records as foreign funds poured money into the market.

Similar reasons bolstered a more modest price rise in Warsaw, while Bratislava's gains seemed vulnerable. Prices firmed in Bucharest too, but Prague paid the price of last week's rally. Ljubljana ended firmer while Zagreb was mixed after earlier gains.
The Central European Share Index (CESI) which measures the price movements of 73 Polish, Czech, Hungarian, Slovenian and Slovak stocks, firmed 1.85 percent during the week.
BUDAPEST
Hungarian share prices surged this week to surpass all previous highs in the bourse's six-and-half-year history. But on Friday profit-taking brought an almost two percent correction.
On Friday, the BUX index closed at 5,032.86 points, up 318.36 points.

"Today's fall was a warning sign," said Kalman Schuszter of New York Broker Budapest. "I expect the market to consolidate at these levels," he said, adding that sideways movements should be the logical and natural aftermath.
WARSAW

The Polish bourse which has risen 20 percent since mid-December to seven 33-month highs, should extend this week's slower growth next week, though a correction looked ever more possible, analysts said.
The main market's all-share WIG index closed at 15,974.6 points on Friday, up 555.7 points or 3.6 percent from last Friday's close. The WIG rose 6.8 percent last week.

"The level of 16,000 points could provide temporary psychological resistance but I think it will be beaten in the near future," said Tomasz Cwintal, an analyst at Bank Gospodarki Zywnosciowej (BGZ) brokerage.

Analysts said continued growth by large-cap stocks such as industrial and trading conglomerate Elektrim, which gained 21.2 percent this week, signalled buying by institutional investors acting on their firms' fresh picks for 1997.
PRAGUE

The Czech PX50 index stagnated this week after a string of sharp gains in the first week of trading this year. Blue chips were particularly sluggish, especially the new year's star performer, power utility CEZ, which peaked at 1,070 on Monday.

"Most people realised some profit and they see the price (of CEZ) a little bit high...so maybe they are starting to be worried that the price has reached a peak," said Ivan Kusacek of Zivnostneska Banka in Prague.

In the broader market, brewer Pivovar Radegast posted some strong gains following an announcement by Britain's Bass Plc last week that it had increased its stake in the firm to 33 percent, and was mulling the possibility of eventually merging it with Prazske Pivovary in which it holds a majority stake.
BRATISLAVA
The Bratislava Stock Exchange saw a week of moderate, gradually growing activity, but brokers warned the growth was fragile due to a constant lack of liquidity.
The 12-share SAX index gained 6.1 points from the rising blue chips' prices and closed at 185.57 points on Friday.
Traders said the market had been expected to decline in the near future, with investors apparently waiting for a drop in the value of the most demanded issues.
"Investors playing on our market are also aware of the fact that there is still only a few of them here," Dusan Sykora of ING Barings said.
ZAGREB

Croatian stocks closed mixed on Friday after a week of strong gains in most issues due to stronger buying and the market was seen as consolidating fully after the country was awarded its first-ever rating of BBB-.
"It is nice to see the market awakening," said Dubravko Zganec, head of trading at Fima, one of the most active brokerages in 1996.
He predicted solid gains in most liquid stocks which are still trading below book value, mainly leading food and hotel firms.
LJUBLJANA
Slovenian shares on Friday reversed from minor falls earlier to finish the week with an overall 3.5 percent gain. The ten-share SBI index firmed 45 points to 1,322.8.
BUCHAREST
Strong buying interest powered stock prices upwards on the Bucharest bourse this week with traders expecting the bullish mood to continue in the first session next week.
Brokers said buoyant sentiment was prompted by a depreciation in the local currency, the leu, which has shed some 20 percent to 4,950/5,050 to the dollar since January 1.
The two unofficial indices, Vanguard SA 's VAB and Bucharest Investment Group 's BIG, rose by five percent and 4.97 percent, respectively, from the previous session.
